feedback: Iteration 0 is the only raced evidence. All 60 trials ended off_track with 0 finishes, progress 0.04 to 0.115, max_error about 0.061 (just past the 0.06 m limit), and exactly one line-loss event per run. The error was nearly identical on oval, s-bend and slalom, which points to a systematic early or start-up swing rather than a track-shape problem. Steering_oscillation was low (about 0.07), so jitter is not the cause. This candidate changes base_speed 1.6 to 1.2, kd 0.05 to 0.2, kp 2.0 to 1.5, and moves the outer sensors to plus or minus 0.05 m. Each change targets the iteration 0 failure. The candidate is valid and not obviously broken, and it is a sensible test of the overshoot hypothesis, so I am approving it to race for telemetry. Be aware that base_speed 1.2 gives a PWM fraction of 0.6, so finishing within 3.0 s (about 1.5 m/s average) is unlikely at this speed. The main score this race can show is progress and line-loss behaviour. Once it races, read progress, max_error and line_loss_events per track first. If max_error is now below 0.05 with progress above 0.5 but completion_time near 3 s, raise base_speed in steps of 0.2 while watching max_error. If the swing persists at the same magnitude on all tracks, suspect the start transient or the fixed motor mismatch, and test ki at 0.5 or a larger kd.
requested_changes: If progress is above 0.5 and max_error is below 0.05 after this race, raise controller.base_speed in steps of 0.2 (1.2 to 1.4, then 1.6) and keep kp 1.5 and kd 0.2 so the speed effect is isolated. Iteration 0 shows that base_speed 1.6 with kp 2.0 and kd 0.05 left the line on every track.

If max_error stays near 0.06 with one line-loss event on all tracks, the swing is probably a start transient or the motor mismatch. Try controller.ki 0.5 (integral limited to +/-2) or raise controller.kd to 0.3, since iteration 0 showed the same error on all three tracks.

If line_loss_events is still one per run, keep the outer sensors at plus or minus 0.05 and try controller.line_loss set to search_left or search_right to match the side the robot drifts toward, since iteration 0 tracked a single one-sided swing.
